plan.disposition: Mini-Plan is FEATURE-only at small complexity per the Phase Matrix; this run is a BUG fix

findings.finding: The Windows-only regression tests (skipIf(process.platform !== 'win32')) never run in CI, since every workflow in .github/workflows runs on ubuntu-latest only — no Windows runner exists. A future refactor of resolveSpawn/defaultRunShim could silently break the Windows codepath with CI staying green.
findings.suggestion: Non-blocking: mirrors a pre-existing pattern already merged in the same file (the ~/.local/bin win32-only defaultRun test, iterate-2026-08-23). Worth a follow-up ticket to add a Windows CI job; out of scope for this bug fix.

findings.finding: defaultRunShim is safe because both current callers pass hardcoded literals
hand-rolled process.env.PATH mutation + try/finally is race-safe under Vitest's worker-thread scheduling
resolveSpawn's non-augmented PATH search is sufficient for every real Codex CLI install shape

On win32, `defaultRunShim` drops the `probeEnv`-augmented environment entirely — `execFile` is called with no `env` option, so the child inherits `process.env`. That's fine for `codex` per the spec's rationale, but the function is exported (re-exported from `readiness-probe.ts`) and documented as a general shim probe; a future caller with a tool whose shim lives in an augmented-PATH location (the exact uv scenario) would silently fail to find it.
findings.suggestion: Either note the "real `process.env` only" limitation explicitly in the doc comment, or accept an optional `env` and pass it through to `execFile`.

findings.finding: The unmocked `isCodexCliAvailable` test passes even if a real `codex` is already on the machine's PATH — the fake shim prepended to `PATH` makes the test non-deterministic in what it proves. Also, mutating `process.env.PATH` is process-global; if this file ever gains `describe.concurrent` or other tests running interleaved, they'd see the mutated PATH. Neither breaks correctness today.
findings.suggestion: Optional hardening: assert the resolved shim is the fake one (e.g. by having the shim echo a unique token and checking via `defaultRunShim` output), and keep PATH mutation serialized.  On the core questions: (1) spec is fully implemented — both call sites (`runtime-chokepoint.ts`, `readiness-probe.ts` codex arm) route through the new `defaultRunShim`, `defaultRun` is untouched, the `deps.run` seam still governs both arms. (2) The `resolveSpawn` null → not-found path, the timeout/ENOENT → `code:null` contract, and the POSIX pass-through all look correct; `parseExecResult` is a faithful extraction of the original callback logic. (3) No new security surface — `resolveSpawn` is the already-reviewed ADR-044 mechanism, and only hardcoded tool names are probed. (4) The Windows tests genuinely exercise real `.cmd` shims and the not-found/error paths; the POSIX pass-through test is weaker (only checks `ok` equality on `node`) but acceptable. (5) No regression risk to uv/python/git probing since `defaultRun` is unmodified.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: approve
